title: Model Source Validation and Runtime Artifact Approval
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: We need an automated, auditable gating flow for new model bundles (weights, tokenizer, config, artifacts) that enforces license compatibility, restricted-weights policy, and minimal provenance metadata before a model is published in the Redwood catalog or pinned for Dedicated/Private deployments.
background: Current onboarding relies on ad-hoc checks by engineering and legal: inconsistent metadata, manual hash verification, and late discovery of restricted licenses or suspect weight provenance. This leads to delays, missed security constraints in Dedicated/Private deployments, and customer confusion when models are pulled or restricted after release.
proposal: Design and ship a Model Source Validation service: (1) ingest model bundle and run automated validators (license classifier + exact license tag matching, signature/hash verification, known-restricted-weight fingerprinting), (2) compute a compliance status and human-review flag, (3) attach a structured, immutable compliance artifact to the model version (license, allowed_for_hosted:yes/no, restricted_weights:yes/no, provenance_links), (4) block publish/pin actions for non-compliant models and route to an expedited legal review workflow.
acceptance_criteria: Automated license scan runs for all incoming model bundles and returns one of: compatible, incompatible, ambiguous with clear reason codes.
Weights are verified by cryptographic hash, and the system flags bundles that match entries in the restricted-weights database (internal denylist) with a rationale string.
Models with 'incompatible' or 'restricted_weights:yes' status are prevented from being published to the hosted catalog and cannot be pinned to Dedicated/Private without an explicit exception ticket.
A compliance artifact (signed JSON blob) is attached to every model_version record and visible in the Console model detail page and via API when fetching model metadata.
Legal and Security can review ambiguous or flagged models via a one-click review queue with links to the original bundle, computed checksums, and suggested mitigations.
End-to-end tests and an integration test in the onboarding pipeline that simulates a license-mismatch and a restricted-weight match with expected blocked outcome.
tasks: Spec: draft validation rules, reason codes, and exception workflow (PM + Legal + Security)
Engineering: implement validator microservice with pluggable checks (license-parser, hash-checker, provenance-parser)
Infra: add persistent, signed compliance artifact storage and RBAC for exception creation
Console: expose compliance artifact on model detail page and show gating status in publication flow
API: add model_version.metadata.compliance endpoint and deny publish/pin endpoints when status requires review
QA: create test harness covering license ambiguous, incompatible, restricted weight, and successful pass cases
Launch: run a one-week audit of recently published models to backfill compliance artifacts and surface retroactive issues

notes: Do not conflate 'ambiguous' with 'compatible' — ambiguous models should always require human review.
Consider integrating with partner provenance services (e.g., modelcard or trust-signature providers) in later phases.
Keep the restricted-weights list separate from open-source license checks; weights may be restricted for policy reasons even if license is permissive.
